scope: Success criteria applicable to static HTML/CSS interfaces with light client-side JavaScript.

source.derived_from: files.zip in this repository - a Markdown/JSON conversion of the w3c/wcag normative source
source.note: The `text` field is W3C normative text reproduced under the W3C Document License. The `static_html_test` field is study-authored operational guidance and is NOT part of WCAG.

excluded.1.2.x: time-based media - replicas contain no audio or video by protocol
excluded.2.2.x: timing - no time limits, auto-updating or moving content
excluded.2.5.1/2.5.2/2.5.4/2.5.7: pointer gestures, cancellation, motion actuation, dragging - not implemented in static replicas
excluded.3.3.4: error prevention (legal/financial/data) - all transactional flows are simulated per Rules.md section 5
excluded.AAA: all Level AAA criteria are out of scope

success_criteria.title: Non-text Content
success_criteria.text: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, except for the situations listed below.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Every img, svg, icon and decorative graphic has an alt or accessible name conveying its purpose; decorative images have alt="".

success_criteria.title: Info and Relationships
success_criteria.text: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Structure is conveyed in markup: real headings, lists, tables with headers, fieldset/legend, label-for on every control.

success_criteria.title: Meaningful Sequence
success_criteria.text: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.
success_criteria.static_html_test: DOM order matches the visual reading order; no CSS reordering that breaks sequence.

success_criteria.title: Sensory Characteristics
success_criteria.text: Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Instructions do not rely on shape, size, position or colour alone ("the button on the right").

success_criteria.title: Orientation
success_criteria.text: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, such as portrait or landscape, unless a specific display orientation is essential.
success_criteria.static_html_test: No orientation lock; layout works in portrait and landscape.

success_criteria.title: Identify Input Purpose
success_criteria.text: The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined when:
success_criteria.static_html_test: Inputs collecting user data carry the correct autocomplete token.

success_criteria.title: Use of Color
success_criteria.text: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Colour is never the only means of conveying information, including link-vs-text distinction.

success_criteria.title: Contrast (Minimum)
success_criteria.text: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for the following:
success_criteria.static_html_test: Text contrast >= 4.5:1 (>= 3:1 for large text) against its actual background.

success_criteria.title: Resize Text
success_criteria.text: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Text can scale to 200% without loss of content or function; avoid fixed px on containers that clip.

success_criteria.title: Images of Text
success_criteria.text: If the technologies being used can achieve the visual presentation, text is used to convey information rather than images of text except for the following:
success_criteria.static_html_test: Text is real text, not an image of text, except logos.

success_criteria.title: Reflow
success_criteria.text: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions for: Except for parts of the content which require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning.
success_criteria.static_html_test: No horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px; content reflows to a single column.

success_criteria.title: Non-text Contrast
success_criteria.text: The visual presentation of the following have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s):
success_criteria.static_html_test: UI component boundaries and meaningful graphics have >= 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours.

success_criteria.title: Text Spacing
success_criteria.text: In content implemented using markup languages that support the following text style properties, no loss of content or functionality occurs by setting all of the following and by changing no other style property: Exception: Human languages and scripts that do not make use of one or more of these text style properties in written text can conform using only the properties that exist for that combination of language and script.
success_criteria.static_html_test: No clipping or overlap when line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter-spacing .12em, word-spacing .16em are applied.

success_criteria.title: Content on Hover or Focus
success_criteria.text: Where receiving and then removing pointer hover or keyboard focus triggers additional content to become visible and then hidden, all of the following are true: Exception: The visual presentation of the additional content is controlled by the user agent and is not modified by the author.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Content revealed on hover or focus is dismissable, hoverable and persistent.

success_criteria.title: Keyboard
success_criteria.text: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard alone; no click-only handlers on non-focusable elements.

success_criteria.title: No Keyboard Trap
success_criteria.text: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component of the page using a keyboard interface, then focus can be moved away from that component using only a keyboard interface, and, if it requires more than unmodified arrow or tab keys or other standard exit methods, the user is advised of the method for moving focus away.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Focus can always move away from any component using the keyboard.

success_criteria.title: Bypass Blocks
success_criteria.text: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple web pages.
success_criteria.static_html_test: A skip link is the first focusable element and moves focus to the main landmark.

success_criteria.title: Page Titled
success_criteria.text: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Every page has a unique, descriptive title element.

success_criteria.title: Focus Order
success_criteria.text: If a web page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Tab order follows a meaningful sequence; no positive tabindex.

success_criteria.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
success_criteria.text: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined link context, except where the purpose of the link would be ambiguous to users in general.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Link text states its destination in context; no bare "click here" or "read more".

success_criteria.title: Multiple Ways
success_criteria.text: More than one way is available to locate a web page within a set of web pages except where the web page is the result of, or a step in, a process.
success_criteria.static_html_test: More than one way to reach a page exists (navigation plus search or sitemap).

success_criteria.title: Headings and Labels
success_criteria.text: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Headings and form labels describe their topic or purpose; no generic "Section" or "Input".

success_criteria.title: Focus Visible
success_criteria.text: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Keyboard focus is always visible with a clear indicator; never outline:none without a replacement.

success_criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
success_criteria.text: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
success_criteria.static_html_test: The focused component is not entirely hidden by sticky headers, footers or overlays.

success_criteria.title: Label in Name
success_criteria.text: For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the name contains the text that is presented visually.
success_criteria.static_html_test: An element's accessible name contains the visible label text, in the same order.

success_criteria.title: Target Size (Minimum)
success_criteria.text: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except when:
success_criteria.static_html_test: Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px, or adequately spaced.

success_criteria.title: Language of Page
success_criteria.text: The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined.
success_criteria.static_html_test: The html element carries a valid lang attribute.

success_criteria.title: Language of Parts
success_criteria.text: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined except for proper names, technical terms, words of indeterminate language, and words or phrases that have become part of the vernacular of the immediately surrounding text.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Passages in another language carry their own lang attribute.

success_criteria.title: On Focus
success_criteria.text: When any user interface component receives focus, it does not initiate a change of context.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Focusing a component does not trigger a change of context.

success_criteria.title: On Input
success_criteria.text: Changing the setting of any user interface component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised of the behavior before using the component.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Changing a setting does not automatically submit or navigate without warning.

success_criteria.title: Consistent Navigation
success_criteria.text: Navigational mechanisms that are repeated on multiple web pages within a set of web pages occur in the same relative order each time they are repeated, unless a change is initiated by the user.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Navigation repeated across pages appears in the same relative order.

success_criteria.title: Consistent Identification
success_criteria.text: Components that have the same functionality within a set of web pages are identified consistently.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Components with the same function are identified consistently across pages.

success_criteria.title: Consistent Help
success_criteria.text: If a web page contains any of the following help mechanisms, and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple web pages within a set of web pages, they occur in the same order relative to other page content, unless a change is initiated by the user:
success_criteria.static_html_test: Help mechanisms repeated across pages appear in the same relative order.

success_criteria.title: Error Identification
success_criteria.text: If an input error is automatically detected, the item that is in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Input errors are identified in text and the erroring field is named.

success_criteria.title: Labels or Instructions
success_criteria.text: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Every control has a visible label or instruction; placeholder alone is not a label.

success_criteria.title: Error Suggestion
success_criteria.text: If an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, then the suggestions are provided to the user, unless it would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.
success_criteria.static_html_test: When an error is detected and a correction is known, it is suggested in text.

success_criteria.title: Name, Role, Value
success_criteria.text: For all user interface components (including but not limited to: form elements, links and components generated by scripts), the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Every custom or scripted component exposes a correct name, role, state and value.

success_criteria.title: Status Messages
success_criteria.text: In content implemented using markup languages, status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties such that they can be presented to the user by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
success_criteria.static_html_test: Status messages are announced via role=status, role=alert or an appropriate live region.
